items.title: Attackers gained access to tens of thousands of internet-connected Fortinet firewalls
items.summary: Hungary's NKI reports an FBI alert on the 'FortiBleed' attack series, in which criminals gained access to tens of thousands of internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on eight Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, including two critical unauthenticated RCEs; Citrix has confirmed active exploitation, so customer-managed appliances should be patched urgently.

items.title: Thousands of wind and solar park systems sit exposed on the internet across Europe
items.summary: Modat and NCSC-NL found 8,547 internet-facing systems at wind farms and solar parks in 35 countries in and around the EU that should not be reachable, ranging from login screens to a turbine control page.

items.title: Chinese Government-linked Cyber Threat Actors Combine Automated and Hands-on Hacking Tools to Steal Sensitive Data
items.summary: CISA, NSA, FBI, NCSC UK and partners from seven governments warn that China-linked actors using Integrity Tech tooling steal sensitive data globally; the FBI seized seven domains behind Flax Typhoon's MicroScan and FishHub tools, active since 2021.

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to start migrating now to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from future quantum attacks, stressing crypto-agility because upgrades take time regardless of when the threat materialises.

items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: CERT-EU flags a critical arbitrary file access flaw patched by Atlassian on 5 October across Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU recommends prompt action on a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability disclosed on 22 September, which F5 confirms is being exploited in the wild.

items.title: What the BPFDoor backdoor tells us about attacks on the network edge
items.summary: Rapid7's Christiaan Beek explains how the stealthy BPFDoor Linux backdoor waits for a 'magic packet' and why its operators target mail gateways and other network edge systems.

items.title: EU cyber and science researchers are testing Chinese AI models
items.summary: ENISA and the EU Joint Research Centre confirmed for the first time that they are testing Chinese open-source AI models.

items.title: 'AgentCorruption' Puts AWS Environments At Risk With Single Prompt
items.summary: A now-patched AWS Bedrock AgentCore flaw dubbed 'AgentCorruption' could let an attacker use a single prompt to one AI chatbot to take over an organisation's entire agent fleet.

items.title: Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients
items.summary: Japanese provider IDC Frontier says a ransomware attack on its IDCF Cloud caused an outage at a data center cluster in eastern Japan used by government clients.

items.title: Dutch DPA fines Uber EUR 824 990 000 for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information on profiling
items.summary: The Dutch DPA fined Uber EUR 824,990,000 in a cross-border case for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information on profiling under GDPR Articles 22 and 13.

items.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware
items.summary: Talos surveys 'AI-analysis evasion': techniques malware authors use to obstruct or defeat automated AI-based malware analysis, including prompt injection.

items.title: Fake ChatGPT and Gemini pages used to steal ad accounts and MFA codes
items.summary: A campaign targeting advertising account managers uses fake ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity pages to harvest ad account access and MFA codes, NKI warns.

items.title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
items.summary: PCI SSC published 'Security Considerations for AI Systems', guidance on protecting data fed to AI in payment environments, defending against AI-assisted attacks and requiring human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data.

items.title: South Korea, Japan buffeted by hacks as AI lowers bar for cybercriminals
items.summary: Reuters reports that South Korea and Japan are facing a wave of hacks as AI tools lower the barrier for cybercriminals.

items.title: Chinese developer makes ARTEX AI agent closed-source after Korean bank hack
items.summary: Reuters reports a Chinese developer has made its ARTEX AI agent closed-source after it was linked to a hack of a Korean bank.

items.title: UK's ASOS says cyber hack accessed customers' personal data
items.summary: UK online retailer ASOS says a cyberattack accessed customers' personal data.

items.title: Anthropic rolls out program for ‘long-term commitment’ to secure critical infrastructure, open source software
items.summary: Anthropic launched a critical infrastructure defense program pairing Claude models, its engineers and threat research with cybersecurity firms to secure critical infrastructure and open source software.

items.title: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
items.summary: Microsoft urges organisations to start testing certificate ecosystems for post-quantum authentication now and describes its PQC TLS Pilot Program.

items.title: Lawmakers warn Google could expose Spirit Airlines data in $10 million AI training deal
items.summary: US lawmakers warn a proposed $10 million deal selling Spirit Airlines data to Google for AI training could expose about 100 million emails, 500 million Teams messages and employee payroll and tax records.

items.title: Meet the German spymaster turned treason suspect
items.summary: German prosecutors accuse a former head of the BND foreign intelligence service of profiting from state secrets through his post-service consulting career.

items.title: Reconstructing AI Agent Activity: Two New Scripts for Forensic Review, (Thu, Oct 8th)
items.summary: SANS ISC released two scripts to reconstruct AI coding assistant activity for forensic review, part of new FOR577 material on investigating AI usage in incident response.

items.title: Red Lion Controls N-Tron 700 Series
items.summary: CISA ICS advisory for Red Lion N-Tron 700 Series switches: flaws allow administrative access to view, edit and upload configurations and can disrupt the switch.

items.title: Swedish DPA fines Miljödata i Karlskrona approximately EUR 160 000 for insufficient technical and organisational measures to ensure information security
items.summary: Sweden's DPA fined IT supplier Miljödata about EUR 160,000 under GDPR Article 32 for insufficient security measures following an August 2025 breach.

items.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 - Day Three Results & Master of Pwn
items.summary: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 ended with researchers earning $1,262,000 for 98 zero-days; the final day included three attempts against the Google Pixel 10.

items.title: UAT-11985: AI-assisted event lures delivering real-time Google AitM phishing
items.summary: Talos details UAT-11985, an APT spear-phishing campaign using AI-assisted event lures and impersonated academic institutions to run real-time Google AitM phishing against Taiwan researchers.

items.title: MATCHBOIL: New tricks, same old evil intentions

items.title: Co-creator of Empire Market dark web marketplace given 40-year sentence
items.summary: Raheim Hamilton, co-creator of the Empire Market dark web marketplace, received a 40-year sentence after pleading guilty to drug conspiracy and agreeing to forfeit over $100 million in Bitcoin and several properties.

items.title: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: Outsourcing data doesn't outsource accountability
items.summary: IAPP column on Asia-Pacific privacy developments arguing that outsourcing data processing does not transfer the controller's accountability.

items.title: A view from Brussels: Short of convergence, can predictability and coherence save the day?
items.summary: IAPP's Brussels column asks whether predictability and coherence can compensate for the lack of convergence across EU digital rules.

items.title: Almost 50 arrested as police target Western Balkan network linked to killings
items.summary: Europol says almost 50 suspects were arrested in an international operation against a Western Balkan drug trafficking network linked to killings, kidnappings and grenade attacks across Europe.

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary: Europol's Operational Taskforce GRIMM reports five arrests in Spain, Morocco and France of suspects organising and recruiting for serious violence ordered from abroad.

items.title: As freezing winter approaches, Kyiv residents look for shelter elsewhere
items.summary: A renewed Russian strike campaign on Ukraine's power and energy infrastructure has some Kyiv residents considering leaving before winter.

items.title: Companies want autonomous IT operations but hesitate to let AI act alone
items.summary: Survey: 90% of companies want to move toward autonomous, agentic-AI-driven IT operations within two years, but 77% say their organisation hesitates to let AI make operational decisions alone.

items.title: EU faces gas supply shortage as winter looms
items.summary: New reports warn the EU's depleted gas storage leaves it vulnerable to supply shortages in a cold winter.

items.title: Giant Taiwan flag flies from helicopter for national day, defying Beijing
items.summary: A giant Taiwan flag was flown from a helicopter for Taiwan's national day, defying Beijing.

items.title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal
items.summary: The UN extended the Darfur arms embargo, while Russia and China blocked a US proposal to expand it to all of Sudan.

items.title: Leader of 764 pleads guilty, faces up to 30 years in prison
items.summary: Prasan Nepal, leader of the 764 violent extremist network that groomed and extorted minors online, pleaded guilty and faces up to 30 years in prison.

items.title: ‘Not great, not terrible’: Why nobody trusts Russia to tell the truth about plague
items.summary: Politico on why Russia's lack of transparency fuels concern about a plague-related incident at a laboratory in Irkutsk.

items.title: EU’s fight to break China’s raw material dominance isn’t going well
items.summary: Most of Europe's mining, processing and recycling projects meant to reduce dependence on Chinese critical raw materials are behind schedule.

items.title: Daily summary - 08.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily summary for 7-8 October, including a phishing wave impersonating Austria's pension insurance with a fake 723-euro benefit promise.

items.title: Hellenic DPA decision on a data breach involving E.E.T.A.A. S.A. as processor for the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs
items.summary: Greece's DPA ruled on a data breach involving processor E.E.T.A.A. for the Ministry of Social Cohesion, citing GDPR Articles 25, 28, 32 and 33.

items.title: How Technology Empowers—and Imperils—Dictators
items.summary: Schneier and Seva Gunitsky essay on how technology both strengthens and endangers authoritarian regimes.
